description:
FILED s465bb (Opus, round 23, 2026-09-03) from the #994 probe battery.  PRE-EXISTING and identical on the base tree (1fed80b), on the branch, and under PCL_OPT=none â it is the coercion table, not an optimizer regime.

THE BUG.  A raw ARRAY value reaching STRING context stringifies as a REFERENCE.  perl gives the element COUNT (an array in scalar context is its count, and string context is scalar context); PCL gives `ARRAY(0x1)`.

  my @a = (7,8,9);
  print @a . "", "\n";            # perl 3      PCL ARRAY(0x1)
  sub f { @a } print f() . "";    # perl 3      PCL ARRAY(0x1)
  print lc(f());                  # perl 3      PCL array(0x1)
  print length(f());              # perl 1      PCL 10   (length of "ARRAY(0x1)")
  print +(f() eq '3') ? "EQ":"NE";# perl EQ     PCL NE

Probe: scratch/arrstr.pl and scratch/arrctx.pl in the s465bb worktree (both run under perl and ./runpcl side by side).

WHAT IS RIGHT ALREADY (measured, same probe): NUMERIC context (`f() + 0` = 3), assignment (`my $v = f()` = 3 â box-set counts), boolean (`f() ? ...`), `scalar(f())`, `defined`, `==`, list context, and the explicit-`return` spelling before #994 (p-return-value's `(not *wantarray*)` + `adjustable-array-p` arm converted it at the RETURN).  So the divergence is exactly the STRING coercion of a raw adjustable vector: `%to-string` / `p-.` / `p-str-eq` / `lc` / `length` treat it as a reference.

WHY IT SURVIVED.  The two spellings disagreed and the disagreement hid it: `sub f { @a }` (implicit tail) handed the live vector out and diverged, while `sub f { return @a }` was converted to a count by `p-return-value` and agreed.  #994 makes the two spellings agree by construction â `p-tail-value` keeps `p-return-value`'s arrayâcount arm, so `return @a` still answers 3 â but the IMPLICIT tail (and every other raw array reaching string context, including the no-sub `@a . ""` case above) is still wrong.

THE FIX, and where it does NOT belong.  It is a coercion-table question: `docs/ir-spec.md` Â§2's to-string rule for a raw adjustable vector.  Do NOT fix it in `%p-leavesub` (the frame exit) â that reads `*wantarray*`, and the `insensitive-call` Kind-A gate deliberately omits the context bind for subs whose returns are provably scalar-rooted, so a value rule keyed on `*wantarray*` there would be right only by accident; and it would leave the no-sub `@a . ""` case untouched anyway.  The one place is the string coercion: an adjustable vector (fill pointer + adjustable = an ARRAY, as opposed to the emitter's simple-vector LIST TEMP, whose scalar answer is its LAST element â `p-list-scalar`) stringifies as its LENGTH.

BAR when it is taken: probe the ten shapes in scratch/arrstr.pl on both emission paths, the full sweep (a coercion change is invisible to corpus-diff), and the op/ companion leg (the s421 rule: a `cl/` coercion/stringification change runs op/).

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 7ea827a6) ===
VERDICT: LIVE -- still wrong as filed, and it is ORDINARY code (silent: exit 0, nothing on stderr):
    my @a = (7,8,9); print "count: " . @a, "\n";      perl count: 3      PCL count: ARRAY(0x1)
  `@a . ""` -> ARRAY(0x1) ; `my $s = "n=" . @a` -> n=ARRAY(0x1) ; `sub f { @a } f() . ""` -> ARRAY(0x1) ; `lc(f())` -> array(0x1) ;
  `length(f())` -> 10 (perl 1) ; `f() eq '3'` -> NE.  Right (= perl): `f() + 0` 3, `scalar(f())` 3, `return @a` then `. ""` 3.
LABEL: silent (already in the subject).

=== DONE (s543e, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21) ===
THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (the brief's question: can the value that reaches the coercion tell an array from an array ref?): AT `to-string`, NO -- the experiment (stringify-value's adjustable-vector arm made to answer the count, reverted) broke five ref-stringification paths of scratch/s543e/p3/refstr.pl: `join(",", $r)` (join's element walk unboxes), a match target (`$_[0] =~ ...` unboxes), box-set's magic-setter argument (`$$q = $ref`), the %ENV store of a ref, and a blessed object's "Obj=ARRAY(..)".  AT THE STRING OPERATOR, YES -- the operand it receives is the emitted one: an array VALUE (an array variable, `@$r`, a sub's tail `@a`, keys / values / grep / map, a ternary arm) is a raw adjustable vector, a reference is a BOX (p-scalar's invariant).  Emission alone could not do it: `f() . ""` / `"n=" . keys(%h)` are call results.  So the fix is at the operator boundary, not in to-string and not at emission.
FIX (cl/): %p-str-operand (inline; delegates to %pcl-scalar-collapse, the one collapse box-set and to-number already apply) read on the operand as received by p-. (slow path), the six string comparisons + cmp (slow paths), %p-str-x-plain (`x`'s left operand -- which also fixes the pre-existing `\@a x 2` = "33": it tested AFTER unbox), the p-.= macro (every regime; a literal RHS unwrapped) and %pcl-str-append, %p-case-map (lc uc fc lcfirst ucfirst), p-length, p-ord, p-quotemeta, p-index, p-rindex, p-substr.  A raw %hash in string context is its key count (perl 5.26+).
PROBES: p3/arrstr.pl (17 rows: the task's ten + keys / values / grep / map / ternary / `$r->@*` / .=) + arrstr2.pl (20 rows of breaking shapes: refs, blessed, "" overload, element refs, "@a", $#a, join, print @a, tied @t, `$r x N`, ==, sort cmp of refs, wantarray subs) + refstr.pl (26 ref-stringify rows): perl = tree on all (PCL's short address ids aside; sprintf's stray warning filed as #5211).
GUARD: Pl/t/transpile-test-11.t row 10, inverse FAILS on the base.  ir-spec §3.2, DECIDED ## s543e.


=== CLOSED at MAIN-READY-104 `8959afae` (the reviewing session, 2026-11-21; s543e): the count is taken by the string OPERATORS on the operand as received (`%p-str-operand`), not in to-string (measured: that broke five internal ref-stringify paths).  Review probes (25 lines: `.` `.=` eq lt cmp x length lc uc index substr ord sprintf, sub results by `return @a` / a tail array / map / grep / keys / a slice / reverse / wantarray, hash and tied-array operands, every reference kind, blessed and overloaded objects, nested refs): tree = perl on all, main wrong on 21.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): a raw ARRAY in STRING context stringifies as ARRAY(0x1) instead of its element COUNT -- `@a . ""` is 3 in perl, and lc/length/eq all follow the wrong answer
